subject.title: [Bug]:  Isolated cron session agent loop continues consuming tokens after run marked "ok"

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default to delete-after-run cleanup, and should existing persisted jobs with omitted deleteAfterRun be migrated or repaired?
rationale: Current main skips cleanup for omitted recurring isolated jobs, but the linked fix changes a compatibility-sensitive default and an open related PR proposes the opposite one-shot-only contract.

options.title: Default cleanup plus upgrade path
options.body: Treat isolated recurring cron sessions as per-run scratch state, update the linked fix to cover existing omitted persisted jobs, and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun=false`.

options.title: One-shot-only cleanup contract
options.body: Reject recurring `deleteAfterRun` and resolve this issue through strict validation plus operator-facing recovery guidance for affected jobs.

options.title: Fresh-create-only fix
options.body: Accept that only new normalized jobs change and document that existing omitted jobs require manual edit or a separate doctor repair.

recommendation.title: Default cleanup plus upgrade path
recommendation.body: Treat isolated recurring cron sessions as per-run scratch state, update the linked fix to cover existing omitted persisted jobs, and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun=false`.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron normalization and SQLite store history makes this the strongest available routing owner for the contract decision.
